land.text: Kokand and its surroundings, the base of the Autonomy

predecessors.note: KA: it claimed to be the legitimate government of Russian Turkestan; the Tashkent Soviet held the governor-generalship

land.text: Kokand, taken by Soviet forces in February 1918

successors.note: The Tashkent Soviet administration, which became the Turkestan Soviet Federative Republic on 30 April 1918 (turkestan-assr).

capitals.name: Kokand
capitals.note: KA: 'The Autonomy was based in the city of Kokand.'

correction.text: 'The Autonomy was based in the city of Kokand'; it 'claimed to be the legitimate government of Russian Turkestan' (KA), a claim the page does not map

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page gives no area and no list of districts, so only the seat is drawn as held land; the claim to all of Russian Turkestan is a dual power with the Tashkent Soviet, not territory. Cliopatria has no row.

ledger.note: 1917: the Fourth Regional Muslim Congress at Kokand proclaims Turkestan an autonomous territory. 'On November 27, the congress resolved that Turkestan was an autonomous territory within a Federal Russian Republic'; a provisional government 'led by prime minister Mukhamedzhan Tynyshpaev'. The land is the researcher's reading (the seat).

1918: Soviet forces storm Kokand. The Fourth Regional Congress of Soviets 'voted to outlaw the Autonomy, and arrest its members' in mid-January; the troops seized the Palace of Khudayar Khan on 11 February and shelled the city after the ultimatum of 19 February.
1918: Kokand surrenders. 'On February 22, 1918, a delegation from the old city met with the Soviet army, agreeing to disarm.'
1918: the Kokand Autonomy ends on 22 February. It 'existed from November 27, 1917, to February 22, 1918'; Ergash's resistance from the summer of 1918 grew into the Basmachi movement.

wars.name: Soviet suppression of the Kokand Autonomy
wars.outcome: Soviet victory: the city taken 11-22 February 1918; the Autonomy's government scattered.
wars.note: TA (the TASSR page) calls the Autonomy a 'rival Turkestan Autonomous Republic' that met in February 1918, a month later than KA's November 1917 date; KA is followed.

certainty.note: Only the seat is a held place; no frontier is described.

sources.title: Kokand Autonomy
sources.note: Proclaimed 27 November 1917 at Kokand, Tynyshpaev and Shokay, dual power with the Tashkent Soviet, outlawed in January 1918, Kokand taken 11-22 February 1918.

sources.title: Turkestan Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic
sources.note: The rival Turkestan Autonomous Republic declared at Kokand in February 1918 in the TASSR page.

notes: Written for batch ia-03-x from two pages (KA, TA). The two pages disagree on the date: KA has the congress and proclamation on 25-27 November 1917; TA says 'in February 1918 the Islamic Council and the Council of Intelligentsia met in Kokand city and declared a rival Turkestan Autonomous Republic'. KA is the article about the entity and is followed. The Tashkent Soviet is recorded under the russian-turkestan slug (it governed the krai until 30 April 1918). Territory is the seat only; a gap-filler could open KA's sources for the Fergana districts the Autonomy held in December 1917.
